exact_guarantee_offers.F: (Y,x,r)=(h,a,F), feasible only when F>=0; it forces both voters to yes
exact_guarantee_offers.K: (Y,x,r)=(ell,a,R_L); its worst admissible return is min{b,(1-nu)*R_L}
exact_guarantee_offers.M: (Y,x,r)=(h,b,P); passage pays P and any admissible rejection pays D

response_exhaustion.K: The weak responder must vote yes. The admissible H responses are pooled no, paying the proposer b, or H type 0 yes and type 1 no, paying (1-nu)*R_L; every weak-no/H profile fails exact type-conditioned IC.
response_exhaustion.M: At x=b, pooled continuation gives the weak responder its minimum and T^Y selects yes; any admissible rejection must use low-only continuation and pays the proposer D.

exact_proposer_security.infeasible_F_rule: If F<0, retain F algebraically inside max{F,K,M}; do not treat (h,a,F) as feasible. Since K,M>=0, S_2 remains nonnegative.
exact_proposer_security.upper_bound_partition: Every feasible offer lies in x<b, b<=x<a, or x>=a; their sharp caps reduce to M, K, and F, respectively.
exact_proposer_security.middle_region_collapse: The strict feasibility identity 1-ell-b>a makes the remaining middle-payment/middle-H subcase collapse to min{b,D}, which cannot exceed max{F,K,M}.
exact_proposer_security.attainment: K and M are generated by feasible offers for every admissible parameter vector, so S_2 is an attained maximum of the three guarantee components even when F<0.

ballot_response_map_after_every_feasible.timing: After every feasible proposal, all nonproposer ballots are simultaneous; nobody observes another current ballot before voting.
ballot_response_map_after_every_feasible.weak_nonproposer_j: Compare j's payoff under the two complete public vote vectors induced by its own yes and no, holding every simultaneous ballot strategy fixed. If yes makes the proposal pass, its payoff is x_ij; if either action leaves failure, that action's payoff is j's subjective discounted N2 value at its own successor posterior. Vote yes iff the yes-vector payoff is at least the no-vector payoff; T^Y selects yes at equality. A nonpivotal outcome does not make the actions payoff-identical when the two published failure vectors induce different continuation beliefs.
ballot_response_map_after_every_feasible.hegemon_type_theta: Compare type theta's payoff under the two complete public vote vectors induced by its own yes and no. If every weak responder says yes, H is outcome-pivotal and votes yes iff Y is at least its discounted N2 continuation after no. If a weak responder says no, both H actions leave failure but may induce different successor beliefs, so compare the two type-conditioned N2 values directly. T^Y selects yes at equality. In every retained weak-veto delay constructor, the high type's continuation is h after either action and exact IC plus P7 require both H types to vote yes; reverse H separation is not inserted as a generic punishment.
ballot_response_map_after_every_feasible.posterior_inputs: The continuation record is N2-EQ-LOW-TYPE-ONLY when its successor posterior is at most nu_star and N2-EQ-POOLING when it is above nu_star. Positive-probability histories obey Bayes; zero-probability histories use the explicitly parameterized kappa_i(s) and eta_i(s,v).
ballot_response_map_after_every_feasible.constant_on_path_weak_floor: Every pooling passage pays each weak responder at least b, never min{b,D}.

proposer_identity_completion.behavioral_branch_weights: For each proposer i, p_{i,L},p_{i,P},p_{i,D} are its endogenous branch probabilities, are nonnegative, sum to one, assign zero to unavailable branches, and may be jointly positive only on the declared L/D locus.
proposer_identity_completion.aggregate_rho_set: Pure assignments give rho_c=k_c/2. If F<=a, every fixed k_P slice also admits continuous L/D behavioral splits; if F>a only the three discrete L/P points remain.
proposer_identity_completion.labeled_completion: For every retained count vector, every assignment of its branch labels to the m recognized proposer identities is retained. Each identity carries its own proposal law, pure ballots, beliefs, and successor N2 record. The global set is the full Cartesian product.
proposer_identity_completion.quotient_rule: Only the downstream H-rent quotient may collapse identity permutations, and it must retain every source equilibrium_id and source hash.

nu0_reporting.empty_category_evaluation: When rho_L=0 or rho_P=0, the corresponding bar_Y coordinate remains the typed category-empty object and its absent product is omitted, contributing exactly zero without assigning a numeric sentinel.
nu0_reporting.prohibition: Never encode an empty category as 0, NA, null, an empty string, or an empty array.

downstream_transport.N6: Transport the entire atomic equilibrium record, its parameter predicates, source cell_id, equilibrium_id, and N2 hash; never recombine marginal payoff or outcome coordinates.
downstream_transport.N7: Use the type-specific H map and R1-event outcome map transported through N6; delay is not terminal failure.
downstream_transport.H_rent_quotient: May collapse only H-payoff-equivalent identity permutations while preserving every source ID and hash.

belief_system.positive_weight_proposal: The weak proposer does not observe theta, so every proposal assigned positive conditional probability has ballot posterior nu by Bayes.
belief_system.weak_vote_passivity: Weak ballots are functions of packages, pivotality, and successor continuation values, not theta; they do not directly update beliefs about theta.
belief_system.public_H_vote: When H's type-contingent vote differs on a positive-probability history, the published vote updates the successor posterior by Bayes before N2 is consumed.
belief_system.on_path_delay: Every retained pure delay constructor has the same H action under both types, so an on-path R1 rejection preserves posterior nu and consumes N2's branch at nu.
belief_system.zero_weight_proposal: Every proposal assigned zero conditional probability may receive an arbitrary ballot belief kappa_i(s) in [0,1].
belief_system.zero_probability_failure_vector: Every zero-probability published failure vector may receive an arbitrary successor belief eta_i(s,v) in [0,1], linked to the specified pure ballots and frozen N2 response.
belief_system.zero_prior_types: At nu=0 or nu=1, strategies and type-conditioned payoffs remain specified for both H types; Bayes constrains only positive-probability histories.
belief_system.subjective_object_distinction: A pivotal weak voter compares x_ij with its subjective continuation at the relevant successor posterior, whose floor is b; a deviating proposer is evaluated under the true pre-proposal prior and receives D under low-only continuation.
belief_system.region_check: On-path delay consumes N2-EQ-LOW-TYPE-ONLY because nu<=nu_star.

equilibrium_records.existence_uniqueness_status: Exists. Pooling makes this top-level coverage cell nonempty. The interface gives the complete parameterized family of local branches, proposal laws, pure ballots, beliefs, and labeled proposer-identity assignments; neither strategy nor payoff is generally unique. Empty candidate branches carry typed proof certificates rather than equilibrium sentinels.
equilibrium_records.selection_status: No equilibrium, identity, proposal, belief, or continuation selection is imposed. All local branches and full Cartesian identity assignments allowed by the displayed predicates are retained. The proposal-level minimum-expected-H tie-break is applied only to payoff ties: pooling and low-only residual equality points obey their binder predicates; delay is retained at C=F for m=2; L/D mixing is confined to its nu=0 equality locus. T^Y governs ballot equality. The only permitted downstream identity collapse is the source-preserving H-rent quotient.

ballot_response_map_after_every_feasible.timing: After every feasible proposal, all nonproposer ballots are simultaneous; nobody observes another current ballot before voting.
ballot_response_map_after_every_feasible.weak_nonproposer_j: Compare j's payoff under the two complete public vote vectors induced by its own yes and no, holding every simultaneous ballot strategy fixed. If yes makes the proposal pass, its payoff is x_ij; if either action leaves failure, that action's payoff is j's subjective discounted N2 value at its own successor posterior. Vote yes iff the yes-vector payoff is at least the no-vector payoff; T^Y selects yes at equality. A nonpivotal outcome does not make the actions payoff-identical when the two published failure vectors induce different continuation beliefs.
ballot_response_map_after_every_feasible.hegemon_type_theta: Compare type theta's payoff under the two complete public vote vectors induced by its own yes and no. If every weak responder says yes, H is outcome-pivotal and votes yes iff Y is at least its discounted N2 continuation after no. If a weak responder says no, both H actions leave failure but may induce different successor beliefs, so compare the two type-conditioned N2 values directly. T^Y selects yes at equality. In every retained weak-veto delay constructor, the high type's continuation is h after either action and exact IC plus P7 require both H types to vote yes; reverse H separation is not inserted as a generic punishment.
ballot_response_map_after_every_feasible.posterior_inputs: The continuation record is N2-EQ-LOW-TYPE-ONLY when its successor posterior is at most nu_star and N2-EQ-POOLING when it is above nu_star. ballot_response_map_after_every_feasible.constant_on_path_weak_floor: Every pooling passage pays each weak responder at least b, never min{b,D}.

exact_proposer_security.low_only_rejection_constructor: If rejection is needed, at least two weak responders vote no, both H types vote yes, the current successor posterior is lambda<nu_star, and each unilateral weak yes is mapped to pooling. exact_proposer_security.attainment: The offer and low-only rejection construction attain min{P,D}, including D=b at true nu=nu_star by a successor belief lambda<nu_star.

ballot_response_map_after_every_feasible.timing: After every feasible proposal, all nonproposer ballots are simultaneous; nobody observes another current ballot before voting.
ballot_response_map_after_every_feasible.weak_nonproposer_j: Compare j's payoff under the two complete public vote vectors induced by its own yes and no, holding every simultaneous ballot strategy fixed. If yes makes the proposal pass, its payoff is x_ij; if either action leaves failure, that action's payoff is j's subjective discounted N2 value at its own successor posterior. Vote yes iff the yes-vector payoff is at least the no-vector payoff; T^Y selects yes at equality. A nonpivotal outcome does not make the actions payoff-identical when the two published failure vectors induce different continuation beliefs.
ballot_response_map_after_every_feasible.hegemon_type_theta: Compare type theta's payoff under the two complete public vote vectors induced by its own yes and no. If every weak responder says yes, H is outcome-pivotal and votes yes iff Y is at least its discounted N2 continuation after no. If a weak responder says no, both H actions leave failure but may induce different successor beliefs, so compare the two type-conditioned N2 values directly. T^Y selects yes at equality. In every retained weak-veto delay constructor, the high type's continuation is h after either action and exact IC plus P7 require both H types to vote yes; reverse H separation is not inserted as a generic punishment.
ballot_response_map_after_every_feasible.posterior_inputs: The continuation record is N2-EQ-LOW-TYPE-ONLY when its successor posterior is at most nu_star and N2-EQ-POOLING when it is above nu_star. ballot_response_map_after_every_feasible.constant_on_path_weak_floor: Every pooling passage pays each weak responder at least b, never min{b,D}.

belief_system.on_path_delay: Every retained pure delay constructor has the same H action under both types, so an on-path R1 rejection preserves posterior nu and consumes N2's branch at nu.
belief_system.zero_weight_proposal: Every proposal assigned zero conditional probability may receive an arbitrary ballot belief kappa_i(s) in [0,1].
belief_system.zero_probability_failure_vector: Every zero-probability published failure vector may receive an arbitrary successor belief eta_i(s,v) in [0,1], linked to the specified pure ballots and frozen N2 response.
belief_system.zero_prior_types: At nu=0 or nu=1, strategies and type-conditioned payoffs remain specified for both H types; Bayes constrains only positive-probability histories.
belief_system.subjective_object_distinction: A pivotal weak voter compares x_ij with its subjective continuation at the relevant successor posterior, whose floor is b; a deviating proposer is evaluated under the true pre-proposal prior and receives D under low-only continuation.
belief_system.region_check: On-path delay consumes N2-EQ-POOLING because nu>nu_star.

equilibrium_records.existence_uniqueness_status: Exists. Pooling makes this top-level coverage cell nonempty. The interface gives the complete parameterized family of local branches, proposal laws, pure ballots, beliefs, and labeled proposer-identity assignments; neither strategy nor payoff is generally unique. Empty candidate branches carry typed proof certificates rather than equilibrium sentinels.
equilibrium_records.selection_status: No equilibrium, identity, proposal, belief, or continuation selection is imposed. All local branches and full Cartesian identity assignments allowed by the displayed predicates are retained. The proposal-level minimum-expected-H tie-break is applied only to payoff ties: pooling and low-only residual equality points obey their binder predicates; delay is retained at C=F for m=2; P/D mixing is confined to its strict high-prior equality locus. T^Y governs ballot equality. The only permitted downstream identity collapse is the source-preserving H-rent quotient.
